source: WHO IMCI 2024 / WHO Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment (ETAT)
description: Unified referral criteria based on chest X-ray findings and clinical assessment

criteria: SpO2 <90% without available oxygen
Severe respiratory distress (nasal flaring, grunting, severe chest indrawing)
Altered consciousness or unable to drink
Suspected tension pneumothorax or massive effusion with mediastinal shift
Cardiogenic shock (hypotension + pulmonary edema)
Massive hemoptysis
pre_transfer_actions: Give first dose of antibiotics (IM ceftriaxone if available)
Position patient upright if pulmonary edema
Send referral note with X-ray findings

criteria: Moderate respiratory distress not improving with initial treatment
New cardiomegaly with symptoms of heart failure
Bilateral pleural effusions requiring drainage
Suspected empyema (fever + effusion + sepsis)
Pneumonia not responding to 48h of first-line antibiotics
Suspected TB with danger signs
New cardiomegaly without acute symptoms (for echocardiography)
Non-resolving consolidation after full antibiotic course (rule out TB/malignancy)
Recurrent pleural effusion for investigation
Chronic cough >2 weeks with abnormal X-ray (TB workup)
Incidental findings requiring specialist evaluation
Resolved pneumonia — confirm radiographic clearance
Mild cardiomegaly on treatment — reassess
Small effusion being managed medically — repeat imaging

pneumonia.manage_locally: Non-severe, responding to oral antibiotics, no danger signs
pneumonia.refer_urgent: Severe (chest indrawing, SpO2 <94%), not improving at 48h

consolidation.refer_emergency: Bilateral with respiratory failure, lung abscess

cardiomegaly.refer_urgent: Moderate-severe, new diagnosis, symptoms of heart failure
cardiomegaly.refer_emergency: Acute decompensated heart failure, suspected tamponade

effusion.manage_locally: Small, known cause (heart failure responding to diuretics)
effusion.refer_emergency: Massive with respiratory failure, suspected empyema

edema.refer_urgent: Moderate alveolar, not responding to treatment
edema.refer_emergency: Acute pulmonary edema with SpO2 <90%, cardiogenic shock

fields: Vital signs: HR, RR, BP, SpO2, Temperature
Chest X-ray findings (attach image if possible)
AI-assisted analysis results and confidence levels
